hints: Focus on working out which hydrocarbon is the alkane and which is the alkene by drawing out R-CH3 and R'-CH3 fully.
Remember that R' gives CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH3, the saturated 2-methylbutane, while R gives an alkene with a C=C double bond.
Recall that propagation keeps radicals going (radical + molecule gives new radical), while termination removes radicals (radical + radical gives molecule).
walkthrough:
**Identify the saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons**

Think like a detective and build the full molecules. Add the -CH3 back on.

$$\text{R'-CH}_3 = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
This has only single bonds, so it is 2-methylbutane, the saturated alkane.

$$\text{R-CH}_3 = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$$
This has a C=C double bond, so it is 2-methylbut-2-ene, the unsaturated alkene.

**Recall propagation versus termination**

Propagation steps keep the chain alive. One radical is used and a new one is made.

$$\text{RH} + \text{Br}• \rightarrow \text{R}• + \text{HBr}$$
$$\text{R}• + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{RBr} + \text{Br}•$$
Termination steps kill the chain. Two radicals join to make a stable molecule with no radicals left.

$$\text{R}• + \text{R}• \rightarrow \text{R-R}$$
$$\text{R}• + \text{Br}• \rightarrow \text{RBr}$$

**Match to the table**

For the saturated hydrocarbon we need R' chemistry and a propagation equation. That is:

$$\text{R'-CH}_3 + \text{Br}• \rightarrow \text{R'-CH}_2• + \text{HBr}$$
For the unsaturated hydrocarbon we need R chemistry and a termination equation. That is:

$$2\text{R-CH}_2• \rightarrow \text{R-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{-R}$$
Only one row has both of these correctly paired.

options.A: Both equations show radical + radical to molecule, which is termination, not propagation. The left column is also written with R, the unsaturated hydrocarbon, not the saturated R' hydrocarbon.
options.B: The left equation is a propagation type (radical + Br2), but it uses R, the unsaturated hydrocarbon. The right equation is also propagation type, but the column asks for termination where no radicals should remain.
options.C: Left side is correct propagation for the saturated alkane R'-CH3: Br radical abstracts H to give a new carbon radical plus HBr. Right side is correct termination for the unsaturated alkene R-CH3: two carbon radicals combine to give a stable molecule.
options.D: The columns are swapped. The left side shows 2R' radicals combining, which is termination, not propagation. The right side shows R-CH3 + Br radical, which is propagation, not termination.
